ℹ️ Disclaimer & Safety Info

✅ Why a seat belt matters

With a seat beltThe belt locks and spreads the crash force across the chest and hips, keeping you in your seat.
Without a seat beltYour body keeps moving at the speed of the car and can hit the steering wheel, dashboard or windscreen, or be thrown out of the vehicle.
Rule of thumbWearing a seat belt can cut the risk of death in a crash by roughly half.

📋 Crash speed vs risk

20 km/h (about 12 mph)No belt: bruises, possible head injury. With belt: usually unharmed.
50 km/h (about 31 mph)No belt: severe injury likely. With belt: reduced, but some injury risk remains.
80 km/h (about 50 mph)No belt: often fatal. With belt: serious, but far more survivable.
🚗 The belt takes two seconds to fasten. A crash takes less than one to change your life.

Disclaimer: This video is an illustrative animation, not a real crash test. The outcomes and risk levels are simplified for explanation and are not exact predictions, medical advice, or a guarantee of safety. Real crashes vary widely with the vehicle, the people inside, the angle and the conditions, and no safety device can protect in every situation.

Seat belt laws and child restraint rules differ by country. Always follow the rules where you live, buckle up on every trip, and use an approved child seat for children.
